title: Controlling rotations of magnetically levitated superconductors
authors: Fynn Köller, Dominik Maile, Joachim Ankerhold, Klaus Hornberger, Witlef Wieczorek, Benjamin A. Stickler
abstract: Magnetically trapped type-I superconductors are promising candidates for precision experiments at the quantum-to-classical borderline, with applications in quantum sensing of forces and accelerations and fundamental tests of quantum physics. Here, we show how the rotational motion of micron-sized superconductors is strongly affected by (i) the diamagnetic torques due to the gradient of the trapping field and by (ii) the gyromagnetic coupling due to Einstein-de Haas and Barnett effects. We show that this allows the three-dimensional alignment of asperhical superconductors in the trap center, as required for future sensing applications and quantum experiments, and determine the resulting librational trapping frequencies. Finally, we propose an experiment to probe gyromagnetic coupling in levitated superconductors and we discuss how it can be used to control the particle rotation.
summary: This paper theoretically models how magnetically levitated superconducting particles behave when subjected to external magnetic fields. By accounting for induced supercurrents and resulting torques from both field gradients and intrinsic magnetic coupling (gyromagnetic effects), the authors show that rotation can be precisely controlled. This control mechanism is crucial for developing next-generation quantum sensors operating near the quantum-classical boundary.
main_problem: The primary goal is controlling the rotational motion of magnetically levitated type-I superconductors for use in high-precision quantum sensing experiments.
main_result: The analysis demonstrates that diamagnetic torques and gyromagnetic coupling allow for the three-dimensional alignment and controlled rotation of aspherical superconducting particles within a magnetic trap center.
method: The authors derived equations of motion by treating the superconductor as an ellipsoidally shaped magnet, calculating induced dipole and quadrupole moments from supercurrents, and formulating the dynamics via a Lagrangian/Hamiltonian approach.
model_or_system: The system involves micron-sized type-I superconductors trapped in a magnetic quadrupole field. The physics incorporates London screening currents, leading to induced dipole ($\mathbf{m}$) and quadrupole ($\mathbf{Q}$) moments that couple mechanical motion (rotation) to the external magnetic field gradient.
key_observables: Librational trapping frequencies ($\omega_{i}$), total torque ($\mathbf{N}$), and the resulting alignment of the particle's principal axes within the trap center.
important_parameters: The analysis depends on the superconducting material properties, the geometry (aspect ratio) of the superconductor, and the strength/gradient of the external trapping field $\mathbf{B}_{	ext{ext}}$.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include treating the particle as a rigid ellipsoid and analyzing the dynamics using harmonic approximations around equilibrium.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the stable trapping mechanism in a quadrupole field, the shielding effect of induced supercurrents, and the additional forces/torques arising from gyromagnetic coupling via the induced dipole and quadrupole tensors.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the physical model (superconducting particle in a trap), deriving the necessary magnetic moment calculations (dipole and quadrupole), formulating the coupled equations of motion using Lagrangian mechanics, and finally analyzing the resulting trapping frequencies and control mechanisms.
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum electrodynamics effects (London currents) with mechanical dynamics (levitation/rotation) in a highly controllable system, providing a platform for testing fundamental couplings like gyromagnetism at the quantum limit.
